open_points.subject: OwnerSession uploaded import file lifetime
open_points.text: M11 says “Everything in it ends with the session,” while changed A16 says “from the session's end until that sweep the upload is reachable by no request.”
open_points.question: Does an uploaded file cease to exist when its owner session ends, or may it survive as unreachable runtime state until the sweep?
options: Drop the upload atomically when the session ends
Detach the upload from the ended session and retain it until the sweep
Retain an ended-session shell containing only the upload until the sweep
open_points.default_guess: Detach the upload as unreachable runtime state and delete it at the next sweep.

open_points.subject: Expired-upload sweep schedule
open_points.text: “the upload of a session ended by its limits is dropped by a sweep that takes the import lock once a minute”
open_points.question: What defines “once a minute,” including the first sweep after startup and the maximum time an expired upload may remain?
options: Run on UTC minute boundaries
Run every 60 seconds from process startup
Run within each rolling 60-second interval with no fixed phase
open_points.default_guess: Run immediately at startup and then every 60 seconds.

open_points.subject: Owner-only configuration token presence
open_points.text: Rule 1 permits “for an owner-only start, none of the four,” but rule 2 requires “every item of rule 1 present.”
open_points.question: How does the presence check distinguish the valid owner-only configuration from a configuration missing all four service tokens?
options: Treat the four tokens as an all-or-none group
Require an explicit owner-only mode item
Require all four tokens despite the owner-only clause
open_points.default_guess: Treat the four service-token variables as an all-or-none group.

open_points.subject: Configuration environment-variable names
open_points.text: “The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin with `REGISTRY_`”
open_points.question: What is the exact environment-variable name for each required configuration item?
options: Declare fixed names for the store, backup location, backup key, owner credential and four tokens
Derive names mechanically from the prose item and service names
Leave names implementation-defined
open_points.default_guess: Declare fixed uppercase `REGISTRY_...` names for every item.

open_points.subject: Configuration well-formedness
open_points.question: What exact syntax and encoding make each path, credential, token and backup key well formed, beyond the separately stated length and path checks?
options: Treat environment values as UTF-8 text and impose item-specific syntax
Accept arbitrary non-NUL environment text, with only the stated checks
Decode secrets from a declared representation such as base64 or hexadecimal
open_points.default_guess: Use UTF-8 environment text, accept arbitrary secret text, and apply only the stated path and secret-length checks.

open_points.subject: Secret byte length and equality
open_points.text: “A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at least 32 bytes long”
open_points.question: How are environment-variable strings converted to bytes for length, equality, constant-time comparison and use as the backup key?
options: UTF-8 encode the literal environment value
Require and decode base64
Require and decode hexadecimal
open_points.default_guess: UTF-8 encode the literal environment value.

open_points.subject: Interrupted store-creation temporary file
open_points.text: “at every start it first removes such a temporary file left by an interrupted start, and no other file there”
open_points.question: How is the store-creation temporary file named or otherwise identified so Registry can prove it removes that file and no unrelated file?
options: Use one release-declared fixed temporary filename
Use a declared prefix and remove every matching regular file
Persist a separate marker identifying the generated temporary filename
open_points.default_guess: Use one fixed, release-declared temporary filename beside the store.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption and container format
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and “it records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it, the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key”
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, key derivation, nonce generation, key-digest algorithm, metadata authentication and file serialization are required?
options: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption container and derive a fixed-size key from the configured bytes
Require an exact-size raw key for a declared authenticated-encryption algorithm
Leave the cryptographic suite and container implementation-defined
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption container, a random nonce and a standard KDF from the configured key bytes, authenticating the clear metadata as associated data.

open_points.subject: Backup audit sequence for a new store
open_points.text: “It records ... the last audit sequence number it holds” and checks “that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number.”
open_points.question: What value is recorded and what does “ends at” mean when a new store has never written an audit entry?
options: Record sequence 0 and require an empty audit log
Record no sequence value and require an empty audit log
Refuse to keep a backup until at least one audit entry exists
open_points.default_guess: Record 0 and require the audit log to be empty.

open_points.subject: Newest-backup status during a backup run
open_points.text: “The owner interface shows the instant of the newest kept backup whose record can be read, or that there is none.”
open_points.question: What must the status read return when it races the rename of a new kept backup or deletion of the previously newest backup?
options: Serialize the status read with backup runs
Return a snapshot from either before or after the filesystem operation
Retry enumeration until it obtains a stable result
open_points.default_guess: Allow a coherent result from either before or after each atomic rename or deletion, retrying if the selected file disappears while being read.
